packages.title: Server
packages.summary: The backend settings for your app: sign-in, data, address and where it is deployed.
packages.description: Holds the settings for your app's own backend, such as how logins are checked, which database it uses, the address the app talks to, the deploy target and request limits. It also lets other packages mark an action to run on your server instead of the phone. It adds no commands of its own. You fill in the settings and the packages that need a server use them.
packages.whenToUse: Include it when your app has its own backend and you want to set its login checking, database and deploy target in one place. If your app has no server code, you do not need it.

config.label: Token audience
config.description: Only accept tokens minted for this audience. Leave empty to accept any.

config.label: Token issuer
config.description: Only accept tokens minted by this exact issuer. Leave empty to accept any issuer whose signature checks out.

config.label: Public key URL
config.description: Where the backend fetches your login provider's public keys, when tokens are signed with a key pair instead of a shared secret.

config.label: Login checking
config.description: How the backend decides who is calling: "secret" uses one shared signing key, "jwks" uses your login provider's public keys, "none" means the backend can never identify anyone.

config.label: Signing key
config.description: The secret your login provider signs tokens with. Copy it from the provider's dashboard.

config.label: CloudFront distribution
config.description: Optional. Invalidate this distribution after publishing.

config.label: S3 bucket
config.description: The bucket that serves your site.

config.label: Hyperdrive connection
config.description: The id of a Cloudflare Hyperdrive configuration pointing at your Postgres database. Create one in the Cloudflare dashboard and paste its id here. Leave empty to connect directly with the database address instead.

config.label: Cloudflare Pages project
config.description: The Pages project name that serves your site.

config.label: Worker name
config.description: What your backend is called on Cloudflare. It appears in the workers.dev address and the dashboard.

config.label: Data storage
config.description: Which database your backend keeps its data in. The value none means the backend serves only code you wrote yourself, with no stored data.

config.label: Where your data lives
config.description: Which provider holds the database: supabase · firebase · convex · neon · planetscale · postgres, or "none".

config.label: Database address
config.description: The connection address of your Postgres database, copied from your database dashboard. It includes the password, so it is stored as a secret.

config.label: Where it runs
config.description: Which service hosts your backend. One button deploys to it.

config.label: Update history
config.description: How long live updates are kept so an app that was offline can catch up when it reconnects. Longer means a phone can be away longer without missing anything.

config.label: Firebase project
config.description: Your Firebase project id. It is needed when you deploy to Firebase, and whenever Firestore is your data storage.

config.label: Firestore service credential
config.description: An access token letting the backend reach collections your security rules keep private. Leave it empty and those internal paths simply refuse, while everything your users do is unaffected.

config.label: Fly app
config.description: The Fly.io app this deploy targets.

config.label: Cloud Storage bucket
config.description: The Cloud Storage bucket that serves your site.

config.label: GitHub Pages branch
config.description: The Git branch of your repository that GitHub Pages publishes as your site.

config.label: Internal job key
config.description: A password your scheduled background jobs use to reach the backend. Generate any long random string; nothing but your own server uses it.

config.label: Backend update key
config.description: The public half of your signing key. It lets an installed app check that a backend update really came from you. Leave empty to keep using only what shipped in the app.

config.label: Largest request
config.description: The biggest request body the backend will read, in bytes. Anything larger is refused before it is parsed.

config.label: Netlify site
config.description: The Netlify site ID or name that serves your site.

config.label: Render service
config.description: The Render service this deploy targets.

config.label: Where your server code runs
config.description: Which provider runs the backend: cloudflare · docker · supabase · firebase · convex · render · railway · fly, or "none".

config.label: Backend address
config.description: Where your app should reach your backend. Change it here when you move the backend, and apps already installed will follow without a new release.

config.label: Internal roles
config.description: Which token roles count as the backend calling itself. Only these may reach internal jobs like queue drains.

config.label: Site build command
config.description: Run this before publishing the site. Leave empty when the site is already built.

config.label: Built site folder
config.description: The folder the site build writes, relative to the project root.

config.label: Where your web app is hosted
config.description: Which provider serves the built site: cloudflare-pages · vercel · netlify · aws-s3 · github-pages · firebase-hosting · gcloud-storage · render · railway, or "none".

config.label: Spend beacon app id
config.description: The app identity the spend doorbell rings as. The dashboard fills this when it mints the beacon key; the two travel together.

config.label: Spend beacon key
config.description: The signing key for the spend doorbell. Set it together with the beacon URL, or the doorbell stays off.

config.label: Spend beacon URL
config.description: Where a spend-ceiling trip rings a doorbell: one signed POST per transition, nothing else, ever. Leave empty to keep the deployment fully silent.

config.label: Spend read token
config.description: A read-only token the dashboard uses to read this deployment's spend meters directly from the browser. It can read meters and nothing else.

config.label: Supabase project
config.description: The project reference from your Supabase dashboard URL. It is only needed when deploying to Supabase.

config.label: Webhook signing secrets
config.description: The secrets your webhook senders sign with, written as name=secret and separated by commas. Repeat a name with two secrets while you rotate one, so deliveries keep arriving during the change.

config.label: Webhook time window
config.description: How far a delivery's signed timestamp may be from your server's clock, in seconds. Deliveries outside the window are refused even when the signature is correct.

packages.title: Share sheet
packages.summary: Let people share text, links and files from your app through the phone's share sheet.
packages.description: Opens the native share sheet so users can send to Messages, Mail, WhatsApp, AirDrop, Files or copy to the clipboard. You can share a message, a link and attachments from your app's files together. No account or keys needed.

packages.title: Watch together

packages.title: SnapConversions
packages.summary: Send purchases and sign-ups to Snapchat as conversions, from your server.
packages.description: Takes one tracked event and sends it to the Snap Conversions API, with email and phone hashed first and only when the person agreed. It runs on your own server and tells you whether the event was sent, skipped or refused. You supply your Snap token and ids, and may map your own events to Snap events.
packages.whenToUse: Use it to report conversions to Snapchat so your Snap campaigns can be measured, such as a confirmed purchase. Call it from your server only; it has no public route and sends nothing without recorded consent.

packages.title: SpeechRecognition
packages.summary: Turn the user's speech into text with the standard web speech API.
packages.description: Adds the browser SpeechRecognition API to your web pages inside the app, because the iOS and Android web views do not have it, and also offers a simple start, stop and abort call. It listens through the microphone, streams interim and final transcripts, and asks for speech and microphone permission the first time. You write the page that shows the text.
packages.whenToUse: Use it for dictation, voice search or voice commands in a web page. Code written for the standard speech recognition API keeps working without changes.
packages.nativeValue: It uses the phone's own speech recognizer and permission flow, which the web views do not expose.

packages.title: SpeechSynthesis
packages.summary: Speaks text aloud with the device voices, or turns text into audio files.
packages.description: Lists the voices installed on the device, speaks text with a chosen voice, speed, pitch and volume, and reports progress word by word. It can also render speech into audio files that your app keeps. You write the text and decide when to speak or stop.

packages.title: Spinner
packages.summary: Show or hide the page-load activity indicator.
packages.description: Puts a centered activity indicator over the web surface and lets you show or hide it from your code. It only draws the spinner and does not decide when to spin: the app shell keeps the loading rules for splash and first load. It follows the live web view across page loads. You decide when to call show and hide.
packages.whenToUse: Use it when you want to show a loading spinner over the web surface yourself, for example during your own long task. You do not need it for normal page loads, which the app shell handles.

packages.title: Splash
packages.summary: The launch screen shown while your app starts, with your logo and background.
packages.description: Shows your logo and background color the moment the app opens, then hands over to your app once it is ready and the first frame has settled. You can set the minimum time it stays up, the fade, the spinner and the logo size. If the customizable splash is turned off or its settings are invalid, the standard launch screen is used. You provide the logo and colors.
packages.whenToUse: It is always part of the app. Use its settings to match the launch screen to your brand; the minimum time only keeps the splash up longer, it never delays your app's start.

packages.title: Key-value storage
packages.summary: Save small settings and values on the device so they are still there next time the app opens.
packages.description: A simple store for things like a theme choice, a language or a last-seen date. Values keep their type: a number comes back a number. Read or write one value or many at once in a single call, list keys by prefix a page at a time, and every change is announced so two screens never disagree. Values stay on the device, with no account or keys needed.
packages.whenToUse: Reach for it to remember small things between launches, such as a theme, a language or the last screen. It is not meant for large files or secrets; use files for big data and a secure store for credentials.
packages.nativeValue: Values live in the app's own native storage, so they stay put across launches and keep their type.

packages.title: In-app purchases and paywalls
packages.summary: Sell subscriptions and purchases with a native paywall and one simple way to check what a user owns.
packages.description: Shows a paywall you design in JSON, runs checkout, restores purchases and tells you which entitlements a user has, in the same shape on every platform. It works through Apple StoreKit 2 or RevenueCat. Use it for subscriptions, one-time purchases and paid features. Needs products set up in the App Store or Google Play, or a RevenueCat account.
packages.whenToUse: Reach for it when your app sells subscriptions or one-off purchases and you want one set of calls for paywall, checkout, restore and what a person owns, on both iOS and Android. If you already run everything in RevenueCat you can pick that as the provider and keep the same calls.
packages.nativeValue: Checkout runs through the real App Store and Google Play payment sheets, and refunds, subscription management and offer codes open the stores' own screens.

packages.title: Stream
packages.summary: Watch your app's logs live from a test device on your own relay.
packages.description: Sends the on-device log, error and diagnostic feed in batches over HTTPS to a relay that you own, so you can watch a test install as it runs. Each session is started after a confirmation, shows a live badge, and can be stopped at any time. It exists only on test builds and never sends data to Despia. You supply the relay and pair the device with a code.
packages.whenToUse: Use it while testing on a real device when you want to follow logs from your desk, or to send a one-off report to yourself. It is not available in App Store builds, and it only talks to a relay you own.

config.label: Enabled
config.description: Master switch for live log streaming on test installs (it never exists on App Store installs regardless of this value).

config.label: Background grace (seconds)
config.description: How long a live session survives in the background before it stops itself.

config.label: Heartbeat cadence (ticks)
config.description: While the wire is paused (nobody watching) or quiet, an empty batch is sent every this-many ticks so the relay's acks keep flowing.

config.label: Relay origin
config.description: The https origin of your own live-logs relay. Sessions started from a pairing code carry their relay with them; this is the standing default for Send report and code-less starts.

config.label: Confirm before streaming
config.description: Show a native confirmation before a session starts. Always enforced on TestFlight and ad-hoc installs; turning this off only affects simulator and debug builds.

packages.summary: Take card, Apple Pay and bank payments with Stripe.
packages.description: Shows Stripe's payment sheet and customer sheet in your app, supports Apple Pay and optional card scanning, and handles bank payments and Connect onboarding. Your server creates the payments and sends the secrets to the app. Works with the Payments package. Needs a Stripe account, your publishable key and, for Apple Pay, an Apple merchant ID.
packages.whenToUse: Use it to take card, Apple Pay, Google Pay and bank payments through Stripe in a native app. Your own server must create the payment and send its secrets to the app; this package never holds your secret key.
packages.nativeValue: Native Stripe sheets give Apple Pay, Google Pay, card scanning and bank linking that web checkout cannot match, and the payment never leaves your app.

packages.title: Supabase Auth
packages.summary: Give every visitor an account from first launch with Supabase and keep it when they sign in.
packages.description: Creates an anonymous Supabase user at first launch, so purchases and progress have an owner before any login screen. When the person later signs in, the same account is linked, so nothing is lost. Needs a Supabase project, its URL and publishable key.
packages.whenToUse: Use it when your app's accounts live in Supabase and you want every visitor to have an account from the first launch, then add email, phone, Apple or Google sign-in later without losing their data. Skip it if your backend does its own authentication.
packages.nativeValue: The session is kept in secure device storage and refreshed for you, and Sign in with Apple uses the native sheet instead of a web page.

packages.title: Error and crash reporting
packages.summary: Report crashes, hangs and errors from your app to the monitoring service you choose.
packages.description: Catches native crashes, frozen screens, errors your app logs, failed package calls and uncaught page errors, then uploads them to Sentry, Datadog, Bugsnag or another listed service. Nothing is collected until you choose a service, and personal data can be redacted. Needs an account and project key with that service.
packages.whenToUse: Reach for it when you want to learn about crashes and errors on real devices, sent to a service you own. Nothing is collected or sent until you call configure, so it is also safe to leave in a build you do not want reporting yet.

config.label: Deduplication window (ms)
config.description: Repeats of the same issue inside this window are counted rather than sent again.

config.label: Project key (DSN)
config.description: The project key from your own Sentry or PostHog account. Despia never sees it and never receives your reports.

config.label: HTTP endpoint
config.description: For the http sink, the https address a batch of events is sent to. Any server you control works, so a small Worker and a table is complete telemetry with no vendor.

config.label: Environment
config.description: The environment name stamped on every report, such as production or staging. Empty follows the build's own channel.

config.label: Provider
config.description: Which provider package receives crash and error reports: sentry, posthog, http (your own endpoint), or console (development only). Leave empty to collect nothing.

config.label: Queue size
config.description: How many events are held while offline. When it is full the oldest are dropped, and the drop itself is reported.

config.label: Release
config.description: The release identifier reports are grouped under. Empty uses the app version and build number.

config.label: Error sample rate
config.description: The share of error events that are sent, from 0 to 1. Sampling is by issue, so a rare crash is never lost to a busy one.

config.label: Redact personal data
config.description: Redacts anything shaped like an email, a token, a phone number, a card number or a home folder path before an event is stored or sent.

config.label: Sink (retired)
config.description: Retired spelling of `provider`; still read as the same choice. Set `provider` instead.

config.label: Trace provider
config.description: Optional: the trace row (for example firebaseperformance) that trace.start and trace.end also start and stop live. Empty means spans stay with the sink.

config.label: Trace sample rate
config.description: The share of performance spans that are sent, from 0 to 1. Off by default.

packages.title: Stripe Terminal
packages.summary: Take in-person card payments with Stripe card readers.
packages.description: Finds and connects Bluetooth, internet, USB (Android) or phone-based readers, then collects, confirms and refunds payments your server created. Use it for point of sale and shop counters. Works with the Payments package. Needs a Stripe account, a Stripe location for the reader, and a server endpoint that issues connection tokens.
packages.whenToUse: Use it for in-person card payments with a Stripe card reader, such as a shop counter or a pop-up stand. For payments inside the app with no reader, use the Payments package instead.
packages.nativeValue: Bluetooth and USB readers and Tap to Pay on the phone need Stripe's native reader software and system permissions, which a web page cannot reach.

packages.title: Terra Health
packages.summary: Pull Apple Health and wearable data into your app through Terra.
packages.description:
Connects Apple Health and wearables such as Fitbit, Garmin, Oura and Whoop through Terra, then syncs and reads the data. Needs a Terra account and developer ID, and your own server to start sessions with Terra's API. It is off by default and you turn it on when you want it.

## How it connects

- **Apple Health** is read on the device through HealthKit. iOS asks the person once, with the purpose strings you set.
- **Wearables** (Fitbit, Garmin, Oura, Whoop and more) connect through Terra's Connect widget, opened from your app.
- **Your server** mints the session token with Terra's API, so your Terra API key never ships in the app.

## Set it up

1. Create a developer account at [Terra](https://tryterra.co) and copy your developer ID.
2. Add **Terra Health** and set **Developer ID**. Leaving it empty keeps the integration off.
3. Write the **Health read prompt** iOS shows when it asks to read Health data.
4. Add a route on your server that asks Terra for a session token for the signed-in user.

| Setting | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| Developer ID | Your Terra developer ID |
| Health read prompt | The message iOS shows before reading Health data |
| Health write prompt | The message iOS shows before saving to Health |
packages.whenToUse: Add it when your app should read Apple Health or wearable data (Fitbit, Garmin, Oura, Whoop) and forward it to your own backend through Terra. It needs a Terra account; if you only want Apple Health data inside the app, use the HealthKit package.

packages.title: TikTok Ads
packages.summary: Measure which TikTok ads bring installs and sales, using the TikTok Business SDK.
packages.description: Starts the TikTok Business SDK at launch, records install and purchase events with TikTok, identifies signed-in people with hashed details and fetches the deferred deep link from before the install. It waits for tracking consent when the Consent package is in the build, and also works as a destination for the Product analytics package. Needs a TikTok Ads account, your TikTok app id and an access token, on phones only.

packages.title: Toast
packages.summary: Show short messages and undo bars that disappear on their own.
packages.description: Shows a small card with a message, an optional action button and an icon, which slides in, waits and goes away by itself. The call finishes when the card ends and tells you how: dismissed, the action was tapped, it timed out or it was replaced, so an Undo button needs one line. packages.title: Text recognition and body pose
packages.summary: Read text out of photos and scans, and track body movement from the camera, on the device.
packages.description: Reads the text in an image such as a receipt or a sign, using Apple Vision on iOS and Google ML Kit on Android. It can also follow a person's body joints from the camera or a video, for fitness or movement apps. Images are processed on the device, with no account or API key.

packages.title: Voice

packages.title: WebExtension
packages.summary: Ship a Safari web extension with your app and share state and a sign-in with it.
packages.description: Packages one standard web extension as a Safari extension inside your iOS app and as a zip for the Chrome Web Store. Your app can push values for the extension to read, lend it a revocable sign-in token, hear messages it sends back, and send people to Settings to switch it on. It is off by default; you write the extension's pages and decide what it does.
packages.whenToUse: Use it when you want your product to live in the browser too, for example to act on pages a user visits while signed in to your app. Skip it if you have no browser-side feature, since it adds an extra target to the app.
packages.nativeValue: A Safari extension reaches the user's real browsing and shares the app's data and sign-in through the app group, which a web page on its own cannot do.

packages.title: WebSocket
packages.summary: Keep a WebSocket connection open that reconnects by itself and never loses a message.
packages.description: Opens named WebSocket connections, reconnects with a growing delay, and keeps outgoing and incoming messages in a durable queue so nothing is lost across a drop or a relaunch. You get connection state to show in your screens and an acknowledgement call to confirm each message. You write the messages your server expects.
packages.whenToUse: Reach for it when your app needs a live connection to your own server, such as chat, live feeds or presence, and messages must survive a dropped connection or a relaunch. For one-off requests use a normal API call instead.
packages.nativeValue: The connection and its message queue live in the native app, so they survive the page reloading and are held through short network drops.

packages.title: WebView
packages.summary: Show any web page inside your app.
packages.description: Adds a web view element that embeds a page from a link, with events for start, finish, failure and messages from the page. The page gets no access to native features; it can only send text or JSON back to your app through window.app.send. It is free and open. You decide what to do with each message.
packages.whenToUse: Use it to embed an ordinary web page, such as a checkout, a help page or a map, inside a native UI app screen. It is not the web app shell for hybrid apps, which makes a whole web app native.

packages.title: Home screen widgets
packages.summary: Put your app on the home screen and lock screen with widgets you design in DSX.
packages.description: Each widget is a DSX document that becomes a native iOS WidgetKit widget or an Android Glance widget. Widgets refresh on a schedule, can respond to taps and be configured by the user. Use it to show the next task, a score or a counter at a glance.
packages.whenToUse: Use it when people should see something from your app on the home screen or lock screen without opening it, such as the next task, a score or a counter. Widgets are glanceable; use live activities for something that runs for a few hours.
packages.nativeValue: Each widget is a real WidgetKit widget on iOS and a Glance widget on Android, so it appears in the system widget gallery and updates on the system's schedule, which the web cannot do.
